messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: p99 latency breach detected for dedicated-pool-eu3 (p95 ~ 180ms -> p95 260ms; p99 ~ 1.2s). Streaming stalls observed, tail spikes at 3s. Alert rules: SLO(s) breached: streaming_p99 > 1s. Impact: several customers seeing timeouts and long streaming stalls. Auto-escalation: paging oncall.
oncall-alice: acknowledging — I'm on it. Gathering context. @sre-bob can you join? :pager:
sre-bob: on my way. grabbing dashboards and recent scaling events.
eng-runtime-claire: ping — saw a lot of handshakes failing in the logs around 14:22 UTC. kv-cache coldpath increased for hotshot workloads.
oncall-alice: current queue depth on dedicated-pool-eu3 is 18k requests; normal is ~2k. Autoscaler did spawn but warmup took ~90s per instance, so capacity lagged. See `autoscaler.events` from 14:20-14:28: many ScaleUpRequested -> ScaleUpStarted -> WarmupCompleted delayed.
sre-bob: copying useful logs:
```
2026-03-14T14:21:57Z pool=europe-east pod=gpu-87 event=scale_up_requested replicas=4->8 reason=queue_surge
2026-03-14T14:23:03Z pool=europe-east pod=gpu-87 event=scale_up_started instance_launch=ok
2026-03-14T14:24:45Z pool=europe-east pod=gpu-87 event=kernel_init slow_init=true kv_cache_miss=high
```
eng-runtime-claire: kernel_init slowness + large model warmup (kv cache) explains streaming stalls. Also seeing head-of-line with long-running low-priority requests holding KV slots.
product-dave: any customer visible reports? @customer-ops-ellen
customer-ops-ellen: yes, two enterprise customers reported degraded chat streaming and timeouts in the last 10m. We put them on incident status page and started retries client-side.
oncall-alice: live mitigation plan:
1) Pause low-priority background workloads on eu3 (evict/marked low) to free queue slots
2) Trigger manual scale with hotshot warmup profile (preload KV and weights)
3) Route burst traffic to failover pool in another region for streaming-sensitive endpoints
4) Apply short-term per-customer rate-limits for non-critical routes
5) Keep customers informed via status page
sre-bob: executing step 1. `redwoodctl queue-evict --pool eu3 --priority low --max=5000` — evicting ~4.2k.
eng-runtime-claire: starting manual scale with warmup profile: `redwoodctl scale-pool --pool eu3 --replicas 12 --warmup-profile hotshot-preload` — initiating. Warmup will still take ~45-60s but preloads KV.
sre-bob: after evict run, queue depth down to 9.6k. p95 moving towards 220ms but p99 still high.
oncall-alice: step 3 in progress — rerouting streaming routes for customers A/B to eu2 via routing policy change. `route-manager apply --service chat-stream --from eu3 --to eu2 --fraction 30%`
eng-runtime-claire: enabling fallback to smaller quantized model for streaming (drop tokens cost slightly) for opt-in customers: `model-router set-fallback --service chat-stream --model gptq-medium-8bit` — applied for customer C.
customer-ops-ellen: informing customers C and D about temporary fallback; both acknowledged. :white_check_mark:
product-dave: any quick wins to reduce tail latency while new instances warm?
sre-bob: yes: reduce batch_max_size for streaming workers to avoid head-of-line blocking: `runtime-config set --pool eu3 batch.max 4` — applied. Also enabled aggressive KV cache eviction thresholds so new warm workers get primed faster.
eng-runtime-claire: added a short-term bypass: new requests matching streaming=true get routed to streaming-optimized endpoints that don't do heavy reranking. This cuts some CPU paths.
oncall-alice: timeline so far: 14:22 alert -> 14:25 evict started -> 14:26 manual scale requested -> 14:30 batch reduction applied -> 14:33 partial reroute started -> 14:36 p95 ~190ms p99 ~650ms, streaming stalls reduced.
sre-bob: at 14:40 UTC, new warm instances ready (6 additional), queue stabilized at ~2.1k. p99 dropped to ~320ms. Monitoring continues.
eng-runtime-claire: root cause analysis (initial): burst of short-lived heavy KV-hitting requests (hotshot) overlapped with autoscale warmup delays. Autoscaler triggered but warmup profile didn't preload kv; combined with large batch sizes caused tail amplification.
oncall-alice: postmortem actions proposed (short list):
- Adjust autoscaler to use warmup-profile detection when queue growth rate > X
- Add prewarm template for heavy KV models (preload kv checkpoints)
- Make evict/priority policy automatic for sustained queue > threshold
- Improve routing fallback automation for streaming-critical customers
- Add an observability alert for kernel_init slow_init events
product-dave: will create a JIRA for customer-visible followups and coordinate communications.
customer-ops-ellen: sending follow-up notes to impacted customers with mitigation summary and ETA for full remediation.
oncall-alice: closing live page at 14:52 UTC. SLOs restored for streaming endpoints. Will schedule full incident writeup and postmortem in #postmortems.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: severity=sev2 duration=00:30:35 mitigations=manual-scale,queue-evict,route-reroute,model-fallback followups=postmortem
sre-bob: adding a quick log snippet for triage:
```
metrics.stream.p99 14:20 1.21
metrics.stream.p99 14:35 0.64
metrics.stream.p99 14:45 0.30
```
eng-runtime-claire: note: long-term we should consider pre-launching a small warm pool for sudden hotshot patterns. I'll draft RFC.
oncall-alice: thanks everyone. assigning follow-ups: @eng-runtime-claire RFC, @sre-bob autoscaler tuning, @product-dave customer comms. :thumbsup:
customer-ops-ellen: thanks team — customers updated. closing thread once postmortem is published.
